As the wavelength of the incident light increases, the responsivity of the photodiode also increases. This is because longer wavelengths correspond to lower energy photons, which are more easily absorbed by the photodiode.

A photodiode's responsivity is also affected by its surface roughness, which can be increased by using a rougher photodiode or by applying a rough coating to the back of the photodiode. A rougher surface area allows more incident light to be absorbed, which increases the responsivity of the photodiode.
